name: Ferrovial
exchange: Nasdaq Global Select Market (also Madrid, Barcelona, Bilbao and Valencia exchanges; delisted from Euronext Amsterdam 2026-09-11)
description: Ferrovial is an infrastructure group that builds roads and airports and then owns and operates them. Its profit engine is the Highways division: stakes in toll roads, chiefly the 407 ETR in Toronto (48.3%) and US managed lanes in Texas, Virginia and North Carolina, whose dividends to Ferrovial were EUR 880 million in 2025. Its Construction division (Webber in the US, Budimex in Poland, Ferrovial Construction) is the largest by revenue (about 77 percent of segment revenue) but earns only a 4.6 percent adjusted EBIT margin. Airports is a developer/investor (New Terminal One at JFK, Dalaman in Turkey) after selling Heathrow and AGS stakes; Energy is small and loss-making. It reports in euros under IFRS, is domiciled in the Netherlands, lists in Spain and on Nasdaq, and is a foreign private issuer, not a US domestic filer.

hq.note: Gustav Mahlerplein 61-63, Symphony Towers, 14th floor, 1082 MS Amsterdam (20-F cover). Dutch N.V.; previously Ferrovial SE (name changed 2026-04-30 per EDGAR formerNames). Company is Spanish in origin.

businessLines.name: Construction
businessLines.how: Fixed-price and cost-plus contracts paid by public and private clients as work is certified; thin margin, but it also builds the roads and terminals Ferrovial itself invests in.
businessLines.description: Civil engineering and building works: Ferrovial Construction, Webber (US), Budimex (Poland, 50.1% owned)

businessLines.name: Highways
businessLines.how: Tolls collected from drivers on long concessions, with dynamic pricing on managed lanes (US revenue per transaction rose far faster than inflation); Ferrovial earns operating results on consolidated roads and dividends from equity-accounted ones, and recycles capital by selling stakes.
businessLines.description: Development, financing and operation of toll roads (Cintra): 407 ETR (Toronto), NTE 1-2, LBJ, NTE 35W (Texas), I-77 (North Carolina), I-66 (Virginia), Autema and others

businessLines.name: Airports
businessLines.how: Equity investment in airport concessions that earn aeronautical and retail fees once open; today mostly pre-revenue (NTO), so near-zero operating profit until terminals open.
businessLines.description: Development and investment: New Terminal One at JFK (NTO), Dalaman (Turkey); Heathrow and AGS Airports stakes sold

businessLines.name: Energy
businessLines.how: Contracted construction and operating revenue from transmission and generation projects; not yet profitable.
businessLines.description: Energy generation and transmission infrastructure development, construction and operation

businessLines.name: Other (headquarters and other activities)
businessLines.how: Internal management fees and small non-core operations; net cost centre.
businessLines.description: Parent company costs, plus other businesses such as UK waste management plants

brands.name: Webber
brands.share: US construction, part of Construction (EUR 7,653M segment)

brands.name: Budimex
brands.share: Polish construction, 50.1% owned at 2025-12-31, listed in Warsaw

brands.name: 407 ETR
brands.share: 48.3% owned, Toronto toll road, equity-accounted; included in the EUR 247M share of profits
